angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 593,432 km at 44.14 pc = 0.18 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 22.6535 +/- 0.0170 mas (same row, RUWE 0.91): 44.14 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.853 +/- 0.021 solar radii from Oddo et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-262 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..134O/abstract): 593,432 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.913 +/- 0.029 solar masses from Oddo et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-262 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..134O/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5310 +/- 124 K from Oddo et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-262 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..134O/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Oddo et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-262 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..134O/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-262.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.537, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
